diagram_math_checks.check: Scalar ring, objects, induction convention and Hom domains
diagram_math_checks.evidence: Statement uses commutative R, finite G, H<=G, R-linear H-module W and R-linear G-module V. F1 and the induction supplier define Ind as covariant functions, not a tensor product. All three pictured objects W, Res_H^G Ind_H^G W and Res_H^G V are R-linear H-modules. Phi belongs to Hom_G(Ind W,V); psi belongs to Hom_H(W,Res V). No field or semisimplicity assumption is used.

Step 1.1 gives eta_w supported on H with eta_w(h)=h^{-1}w, and verifies covariance. Pointwise operations in the supplier show w -> eta_w is R-linear. Step 2.1 proves eta_(h w)=h eta_w, so eta_W:W -> Res Ind W is an H-map; it is not claimed to be a G-map.

Steps 1.2 and 2.2 give Phi=beta(psi):Ind W -> V by sum over a finite left transversal T containing e, and prove G-equivariance with x^{-1}t=t′h. Each action and psi is R-linear, so the finite sum is R-linear. Restricting Phi gives the displayed H-map Res Phi:Res Ind W -> Res V.

The sole asserted relation is (Res Phi) composed with eta_W = psi. Evaluated at w it is beta(psi)(eta_w)=psi(w), exactly step 3.1. Any G-map satisfying that relation has alpha(Phi)=psi by step 2.1, and step 3.2 yields Phi=beta(psi). The top arrow points right, vertical arrow down, and diagonal down-right; the two paths have the same source W and target Res V.

The original seven numbered proof steps and all original source bytes are preserved as an exact prefix. The final Remarks explicitly state independence; the figure is an illustration of the already established inverse-map calculation.
